why: the B2 certification matrix registers the raw sha256 of its own four new source files as evidence, so a fresh checkout must reproduce them byte-for-byte; with core.autocrlf=true and no eol attribute a checkout injects CRLF

pin_set.scoping_note: still scoped to registered byte containers only; a blanket '* -text' was rejected because 34 CRLF *.sh files under scripts/ would have their blobs rewritten

superseded_records_not_rewritten.note: already superseded by B1_BYTE_FREEZE.json; not rewritten there and not rewritten here

superseded_records_not_rewritten.field: pin_set.file sha256 implied by its pin list (6+2 = 8 pins)
superseded_records_not_rewritten.action: B1_BYTE_FREEZE.json stays byte-intact as the record of that commit; the 12-pin set is carried forward here as a new version
superseded_records_not_rewritten.reason: the pin set grew from 8 to 12 files, which necessarily changes the .gitattributes content

verification_required_after_commit: git archive HEAD <each pinned path> must reproduce the registered sha256 exactly; run after the commit that adds these pins, because git archive reads attributes from the committed tree
